| [LIT-2333](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2333.md) v2 | Metamorphic Testing: A Review of Challenges and Opportunities | Tsong Yueh Chen, Fei-Ching Kuo, Huai Liu, Pak-Lok Poon, Dave Towey, T. H. Tse and Zhi Quan Zhou (2018), ACM Computing Surveys 51(1), article 4, DOI 10.1145/3143561. A review by the originators of metamorphic testing: where no practical oracle checks one output, a program is checked against metamorphic relations, necessary properties of the target algorithm across two or more related inputs and their outputs. It formalizes the relations, corrects four common misreadings, and is explicit that the method alleviates the oracle problem and "can never completely solve it", since the relations are necessary, not sufficient. | [LIT-2479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2479.md) v3 | COPE - Automating Coupled Evolution of Metamodels and Models | Herrmannsdoerfer, Benz and Juergens (2009), COPE - Automating Coupled Evolution of Metamodels and Models. When a modeling language's metamodel changes, the existing models must be migrated. The paper calls this pairing "coupled evolution". **The requirements study.** An earlier study of two industrial metamodel histories found: - about half the changes were metamodel-only; - more than three quarters of the coupled changes were metamodel-independent, so they could be reused; - the rest were metamodel-specific; - none were model-specific. This yields two requirements: reuse and expressiveness. **COPE's answer.** A language evolves through a sequence of coupled transactions, each pairing a metamodel adaptation with its model migration. There are two kinds: - **Reusable** transactions, drawn from a library: rename, extract class, generalize reference, and so on. - **Custom** transactions, written in a Turing-complete language. Read for the exchange "luria experiment design". | Active — Read on 2026-11-12 ([NOTE-1811](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1811.md)) from https://wwwbroy.in.tum.de/publ/papers/ECOOP2009_herrmannsdoerfer_cope_automating_coupled.pdf. |

| [LIT-3127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3127.md) | Refinement Types for ML | Freeman & Pfenning (1991), PLDI '91, ACM SIGPLAN, pp. 268–277. A system of subtypes for ML: the programmer declares recursive subtypes (rectype) of a datatype, such as singleton lists or bitstrings without leading zeros; these close under intersection and union into a finite lattice for each datatype, and refinement types are inferred by abstract interpretation over it, given only to programs already well-typed in ML. The language of programs is unchanged; an annotation is accepted only when the inferred refinement lies below it. Read in [NOTE-2350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2350.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md)'s test of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md); the reading is [THEORY-2259](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2259.md). | Active — read in full 2026-11-22 ([NOTE-2350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2350.md)) from the authors' preprint on Frank Pfenning's faculty page at Carnegie Mellon, not the version of record; worth reading as the paper that introduced refinement types, the record's first reading of a type system in which a type is narrowed by subtypes every value of which already has the type it refines. |
| [LIT-3128](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3128.md) | Intersection Types and Computational Effects | Davies & Pfenning (2000), ICFP '00, ACM SIGPLAN, pp. 198–208. Intersection types, the form of type refinement types need, are unsound once a language has mutable references; restricting intersection introduction to values, as Standard ML restricts polymorphism, and dropping the distributivity law of subtyping restores soundness (progress and preservation are proved). Since type inference for the result is "most likely undecidable" and principal types do not exist, the authors give a bidirectional checker: the programmer ascribes types, chiefly to function definitions, terms are checked against them or have types synthesized, and ascriptions are erased, with no coercion inserted. Read in [NOTE-2351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2351.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md)'s test of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md); the reading is [THEORY-2260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2260.md). | Active — read in full 2026-11-22 ([NOTE-2351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2351.md)) from the authors' copy on Frank Pfenning's faculty page at Carnegie Mellon, the published text with the ACM permission notice, paginated 1 to 11; worth reading as the paper that introduced bidirectional checking for intersection and refinement types, and the record's first reading of a type system in which checking is a mode of its own. |
| [LIT-3130](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3130.md) | Liquid Types | Rondon, Kawaguchi & Jhala (2008), PLDI '08, ACM SIGPLAN, pp. 159–169. Dependent types {ν : B \| φ} for ML, inferred without annotations by restricting φ, at λ-abstractions, conditionals, lets and polymorphic instantiation, to conjunctions of logical qualifiers from a finite set the programmer supplies. Hindley-Milner types give templates, the typing rules give subtyping constraints, and predicate abstraction weakens the assignment of every qualifier until the constraints hold, giving the strongest conjunction that a conservative check in a decidable logic can verify. A program with no such type is reported, not changed. DSOLVE cuts the annotation that DML's array-bounds benchmarks needed from 31% of program text to under 1%. Read in [NOTE-2353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2353.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md)'s test of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md); the reading is [THEORY-2262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2262.md). | Active — read in full 2026-11-22 ([NOTE-2353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2353.md)) from the authors' copy linked from Ranjit Jhala's research page; worth reading as the predicate form of refinement types, {ν : B \| φ}, and as the paper that makes it inferable by restricting φ, where a type must be inferred, to conjunctions of a finite set of qualifiers. |

| [LIT-3232](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3232.md) | Intuitionistic Type Theory | Martin-Löf, P. (1984), Intuitionistic Type Theory, notes by Giovanni Sambin of lectures given in Padua in June 1980, Bibliopolis, Naples (Studies in Proof Theory). Four forms of judgement, A set, A = B, a ∈ A and a = b ∈ A, each read four ways: a set and its element, a proposition and its proof, an intention and its fulfilment, a problem and its solution, with "a is a program ... which meets the specification A" (p. 6). A set is defined by how its canonical elements are formed; an element is a method that yields one; propositions and sets are identified. A proof of an existential is a pair of a witness and a proof that it satisfies the property, and the set of a ∈ A such that B(a) has such pairs as its elements, "the witnessing information" (p. 53). Universes are sets of codes of sets, closed under the set-forming operations; there is no set of all sets, and U is not an element of U. Read in [NOTE-2419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2419.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md)'s test of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md); the reading is [THEORY-2307](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2307.md). | Active — read 2026-11-25 (Skimmed: the introduction, the explanations of the forms of judgement, propositions as sets, the cartesian product and disjoint union with their applications, the notion of such that and universes closely, pp. i–54, 64, 69–70 and 87–91; the rest at the level of rules and examples) from a scan hosted by a Carnegie Mellon course, OCR'd; worth reading as the source of the judgement forms and the propositions-as-sets reading on which [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md)'s test of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md) turns, and as the place where a set read as a specification and its elements as programs that meet it is said in so many words. |
